q: How many interlocking rings appear on the Olympic flag?
note: The six colours, counting the white background, were chosen because every national flag of the day contained at least one of them.

q: Which city hosted the first modern Olympic Games, in 1896?
note: Winners there were handed a silver medal and an olive branch, as gold for first place only arrived later.

q: Which Winter Olympic sport has team-mates sweeping the ice in front of a sliding stone?
note: The granite stones weigh around 44 pounds each, and the finest have long been quarried from a single Scottish island, Ailsa Craig.

q: How many separate events make up the Olympic decathlon?
note: The name comes from the Greek for ten contests, and they are spread over two exhausting days.

q: How many years apart are the Summer Olympic Games normally held?
note: The four-year gap itself has a name, borrowed from the ancient Greeks: an Olympiad.

q: In which country were the ancient Olympic Games held?
note: They took place at Olympia in honour of Zeus, with the first recorded games traditionally dated to 776 BC.

q: The traditional Olympic motto is Faster, Higher, and which third word?
note: In the original Latin it is Citius, Altius, Fortius, and a fourth word meaning Together was added in 2021.

q: Which Spanish city hosted the 1992 Summer Olympics?
note: Its opening ceremony ended with an archer firing a flaming arrow over the cauldron to light it.

q: How many miles long is an Olympic marathon?
note: The oddly precise distance was fixed after the 1908 London Games and made the official standard in 1921.

q: Which Winter Olympic sport combines cross-country skiing with rifle shooting?
note: Competitors shoot both lying down and standing up, and every miss costs them a penalty loop or a time penalty.

q: Which Olympic sport is contested with weapons called the foil, the epee and the sabre?
note: The three weapons have different target areas, and with the epee the entire body counts.

q: Which French alpine town hosted the first Winter Olympics, in 1924?
note: It was billed at the time as an International Winter Sports Week and only later recognised as the first Winter Games.

q: The Olympic Games of 1940 and 1944 were cancelled because of what?
note: Tokyo had been due to host in 1940, and it eventually got its Games 24 years later.

q: In which Olympic sliding sport do athletes race head-first down an ice track?
note: Its close cousin the luge is raced feet-first, which competitors insist is the less frightening option.

q: Which Japanese city became the first Asian host of the Summer Olympics, in 1964?
note: The country opened its first bullet train line just nine days before the opening ceremony.

q: Which Brazilian city hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics, the first held in South America?
note: Golf returned to the programme at those Games after an absence of well over a century.

q: Which French baron founded the modern Olympic Games?
note: He also designed the five-ring flag, and his heart is buried at ancient Olympia.

q: Olympic gold medals are made mostly of which metal?
note: They are silver medals with a thin gold plating, as the last solid gold ones were handed out in 1912.

q: Which Winter Olympic event combines ski jumping with cross-country skiing?
note: It has appeared at every Winter Olympics since the very first Games in 1924.

q: The three curved shapes that form the symbol of the Paralympic Games are known by what name?
note: Agito is Latin for I move, which chimes with the Paralympic motto, Spirit in Motion.
